lines: A fishing rod. The ship’s old rod, with line still on the reel and a rusty hook on the end.
Not a boat. Not a radio. A fishing rod.
Well. I am hungry, and it is what I have.
One fish. Not much of a fish, but I caught it, and I am going to eat it.
Nobody is coming down the beach. No sail, no smoke, all the way round.
So: I have a rod, and the sea has fish in it. I suppose I fish.
A hook I made myself, out of a shell off the beach. It is not much of a hook.
But it is on the line, and the line is in the water. Bait on, cast out, wait, watch the float.
When in doubt, cast it out.
Somebody else was here.
Somebody else woke up on this beach, and on their third day they were already making knives. They wrote it down, corked it in a bottle and let the tide have it. For whoever came next.
For me, I suppose.
Another of their pages, just when I needed it. The tide keeps bringing them in the moment I am stuck.
I have decided not to ask why. I just keep casting.
Still here.
I half expected to wake up on a ship’s deck with someone shaking me. Instead: sand fleas, the same old rod, and the tide going out.
The fish do not know I am stranded. They just keep biting. I may as well keep fishing.
Dark. Not one light on the water, all the way round.
I am trying not to think about how far it is to anywhere.
The sea is very loud at night.
Ten fish. I counted.
I know almost nothing about fishing. A hook goes in a mouth, and that is about the end of it.
But every fish shows me something, if I pay attention.
Three kinds of fish off the same few rocks. Same bait, same water, completely different animals.
I have started to wonder what else is down there.
The little striped ones have eaten more of my bait than I have eaten fish.
I have decided they are doing it on purpose.
Lost one. I felt it shake its head twice, and then the hook came back to me empty.
I am angrier about that fish than I have been about anything since the storm. Which is probably a good sign.
Third morning. I scratched three lines into a palm at camp.
I am not going to be someone with a hundred lines on a tree. I am going to be someone who gets off.
I have stopped jumping at every twitch of the line. My hands know the cast now.
Out, wait, watch. While I am doing that, the part of my head that worries goes quiet for a while.
I have started to think of whoever wrote the pages as a friend. A friend who is always a few weeks ahead of me.
They never sign anything. I wish I knew their name.
A real rod. All right: a long cane with a line on it. But it bends like a real one, and it throws like one.
The reef edge, then.
I talk to the fish now. Mostly about the weather, which is always the same.
They are good listeners. Better than some people I could name.
Fifty fish.
Somewhere along the way I stopped being someone stranded on an island who fishes, and became someone who fishes, stranded on an island.
It is a small difference. I think it matters.
A fire of my own, and fish cooked on it. I sat up late just to watch it.
It is the first time this place has felt like somewhere a person could live.
A week, near enough. The island has started to feel less like something that happened to me and more like a place I live.
Which is exactly why I need to leave it.
“Not with this gear. Not on this island.”
They were not giving up. They were getting ready to go.
Then so am I.
A hundred fish.
If anyone ever asks what I did on the island, that is the answer. I fished. I kept fishing. And every one of them got me a little further off this beach.
West-south-west. Smoke on the horizon some evenings, and a port two days off.
It took them seventy-one days. I have been here {days}.
A hull. It floats. I sat on it in the lagoon for an hour, just to be sure.
It is the best thing I have ever made.
Everything is ready. I walked the whole island one last time.
I will miss the point at sunset. I will not miss the striped thieves.
When in doubt, cast off.
People. Noise. Somebody frying fish on a cart and shouting about it.
I stood on the pier for a long time, just listening to voices that were not mine.
Then I went and found somewhere to fish. Old habits.
